crime_highlights: The appellant was convicted of one count of importing cocaine contrary to s. 6(1) of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act
She was returning from St. Maarten, travelling alone
She had approximately 3.2 kilograms of cocaine strapped to her body with a body pack girdle
rationale_highlights: The appellant is a Black single mother who grew up in and out of foster care
her reasons demonstrate that she considered and gave appropriate mitigating weight to the evidence and the appellant’s submissions concerning the effects of anti-Black racism on her circumstances
there is no basis to suggest that the systemic factors reviewed in Morris were ignored in crafting the sentence
note: Appeal court says trial judge gave appropriate mitigating weight; effect is implicit.

crime_highlights: The complainant reacted by slashing the appellant with an exacto knife
Both the appellant and complainant punched and threatened to kill each other.
The altercation resulted in the complainant suffering a broken nose.
the appellant instructed her to go into the washroom to clean herself up and threatened to kill her when she protested
The appellant chased her around the apartment with a stick until she returned to the washroom
rationale_highlights: I agree that the IRCA is relevant to understanding the appellant’s moral culpability for his criminal antecedents
the IRCA in this case directly links these social determinants with the appellant’s personal life, which aids in mitigating the appellant’s moral culpability for his criminal behavior
Of course, the appellant’s moral culpability is mitigated, in part, by the evidence adduced in the IRCA
The report discusses how the appellant endured systemic racism in the past
note: Culpability mitigated in part but indeterminate sentence still imposed.

crime_highlights: The deceased and the appellant were long-time friends and were playing a game of Russian Roulette with a loaded firearm.
The appellant admitted that he deliberately and willfully discharged the firearm at the deceased and that this unlawful act caused the deceased’s death.
rationale_highlights: the appellant also submitted that the sentencing judge did not consider his Indigenous background in arriving at a fit sentence
The appellant has provided information that he is Indigenous and has participated in Indigenous programming while incarcerated
we are nonetheless satisfied that to give effect to the remedial purpose of s. 718.2(e) of the Criminal Code the appellant’s sentence should be reduced a further 6 months
note: No Gladue report; court reduces sentence 6 months for s. 718.2(e).
